title: $\mathcal O_{F,X}$ is finite free over $\mathcal O_{E,X}$
statement:
Let $E\subset F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb$, of degree $d=[F:E]$, and
let $X$ be a scheme. Then a choice of $\cO_E$-basis $b_1,\dots,b_d$ of $\cO_F$ induces
isomorphisms of $\cO_{E,X}$-modules, resp. $E_X$-modules,
$$
\cO_{E,X}^{\,d}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\cO_{F,X},\qquad E_X^{\,d}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }F_X,
\qquad (a_i)\mapsto\textstyle\sum_ia_ib_i ,
$$
compatible with the maps $\cO_{E,X}\to E_X$ and $\cO_{F,X}\to F_X$ and with inverse image
along morphisms of schemes. In particular $\cO_{F,X}$ and $F_X$ are flat
([lem-sfb-subfield-flat]).

proof.text: An integral basis exists by [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis]. Fix any such basis. Since $|\ell|=\ell^{-1}<1$, multiplying an element of $F$, or finitely many relation coefficients in $E$, by a sufficiently large $\ell$-power makes them integral. Integral spanning and independence therefore give an $E$-basis of $F$.

source.place: opening sentence: basis existence and field rank

proof.text: [lem-sfb-condensed-subfield-basis] makes the field coordinate map $c:F\to E^d$ a homeomorphism. The integral basis gives $c^{-1}(\mathcal O_E^d)=\mathcal O_F$. Restrict $c$ and its inverse to these subspaces. On every profinite $S$, composition with these inverse maps identifies $C(S,\mathcal O_F)$ with $C(S,\mathcal O_E)^d$; the formulas commute with precomposition and pointwise scalar multiplication.

The cited sheafification theorem makes both abelian-sheaf categories abelian. For the sheafified tensor, the strong monoidal left adjoint $p_X^*$ preserves finite colimits and is additive by the cited preservation lemmas. Apply [lem-sfb-monoidal-finite-free-transport]: $\Psi_{X,0}:\mathcal O_{E,X}^d\cong\mathcal O_{F,X}$ has summands $p_X^*(a\mapsto ab_i)$.

source.place: Apply the additive monoidal functor p_X^*

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-localized-basis-coefficients] at $t=\ell$. The cited localization isomorphisms give $\Psi_{X,1}:E_X^d\cong F_X$ and its square with $\mathcal O\to E$. The square of coefficient inclusions commutes on continuous functions, hence after $p_X^*$. Uniqueness in the new lemma identifies its scalar map with the specified $E_X\to F_X$.

source.place: Invert ell and retain the integral-to-field square

proof.text: For $f:X\to Y$, naturality of $\alpha:f^*p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ on each multiplication map $t_i:a\mapsto ab_i$ says $\alpha_T f^*p_Y^*(t_i)=p_X^*(t_i)\alpha_R$. This gives the integral summand squares, hence the integral square by the coproduct property. Applying [lem-sfb-monoidal-finite-free-transport] to the field basis isomorphism of [lem-sfb-condensed-subfield-basis] shows that the rational maps $p_X^*(E\to F,a\mapsto ab_i)$ are the summands of an $E_X$-linear map $E_X^d\to F_X$; they extend the integral summands ($p_X^*$ of the commuting point-level square), so the uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-localized-basis-coefficients] identifies this map with $\Psi_{X,1}$; the same equation gives their squares.

For either finite-free pair $A\to B$, namely $\mathcal O_{E,X}\to\mathcal O_{F,X}$ with $\Psi_{X,0}$ or $E_X\to F_X$ with $\Psi_{X,1}$, [lem-sfb-finite-free-scalar-coordinates] gives a natural isomorphism of $A$-module valued functors $\operatorname{Res}(B\otimes_A-)\cong(-)^d$. Apply [lem-sfb-scalar-coordinate-limit-criterion] on the small pro-étale site of $X$ with $T=B\otimes_A-$ of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]: $T$ preserves every finite limit, including the empty one. Thus both scalar extensions preserve finite limits, which is the asserted flatness.

source.place: flatness conclusion: finite tensor coordinates and sectionwise limits
